problem: V&L models, including VLN agents, rely on visual encoders pre-trained on small, manually annotated datasets such as ImageNet classification or Visual Genome detection (e.g., BUTD). These encoders are limited to fixed label sets and are costly to scale. CLIP, trained on web image-text pairs, is strong zero-shot on vision tasks but performs at chance level when applied zero-shot to reasoning-heavy V&L tasks like VQA.
motivation: Recent work finds the visual representation is the performance bottleneck of V&L models. CLIP's visual encoder is learned from 400M noisy web image-caption pairs with language supervision, so it scales cheaply and is not tied to predefined classes. The authors hypothesize that swapping CLIP's visual encoder into existing deep-interaction V&L models, rather than using CLIP zero-shot, will transfer this advantage to VQA, captioning, VLN and V&L pre-training.
key_idea: Replace the ImageNet- or detection-pretrained visual encoder of existing V&L models (including the EnvDrop VLN agent) with CLIP's visual encoder, either plugged directly into task-specific fine-tuning (CLIP-ViL) or combined with LXMERT-style V&L pre-training with an unfrozen CLIP backbone (CLIP-ViLp).
insight: Contrastive language-supervised visual features transfer better than classification- or detection-supervised ones, and the gain survives pooling to one vector per view. In VLN (Table 9), detection-trained grid features (Grid-Res50 47.6 SR / 44.7 SPL) are no better than ImageNet-Res152 (48.2/44.4), whereas CLIP-Res50 gives 52.6/47.4; so the gain comes from CLIP's image-text training, not regional knowledge, which pooling destroys. CLIP-ViT-B works well in VLN when its [CLS] vector is used (52.5/47.7, best BT-agent SPL among smaller models) but collapses when its patch grid is used in VQA/captioning (51.38 VQA test-dev with Pythia, 58.0 CIDEr), consistent with its near-zero VG detection AP (0.03 vs 3.14 for ImageNet-Res50) and weaker Grad-CAM localization. Other findings: larger CLIP backbones scale monotonically; unfreezing CLIP during V&L pre-training yields larger gains than frozen BUTD (+9.26 vs +5.72 VQA test-dev, Table 8); applying the usual VG detection fine-tuning to CLIP hurts (-5.54 with Pythia).
method: CLIP visual encoder swap: replace ImageNet/BUTD encoders with CLIP-Res50, CLIP-Res101, CLIP-Res50x4 or CLIP-ViT-B. Grid features are taken from the last ResNet layer before pooling, or from reshaped ViT patch tokens (VQA, captioning).

CLIP-ViL for VLN: EnvDrop / Speaker-Follower attentive LSTM agent (language LSTM_L + action LSTM_A attending over panoramic views and instruction). Each of the 36 panoramic views is encoded as a single CLIP vector (attention-pooled output for ResNet, [CLS] for ViT), linearly projected and L2-normalized as in CLIP. Features are pre-extracted and frozen.

VLN training: R2R-EnvDrop hyperparameters, with or without back-translation (BT-agent) augmentation. For RxR, the processed multilingual data of Li et al. 2021a (Stanza tokenizers) is used, max instruction length is raised to 160, and the imitation-learning ratio goes from 0.2 to 0.4, under a mono-lingual setup.
CLIP-ViL for VQA/captioning: CLIP grid features feed Pythia/MCAN (VQA) and a Luo-2020 Transformer captioner trained with SCST; there is no V&L pre-training.

CLIP-ViLp: single-stream BERT-base Transformer over text subwords plus CLIP grid patches (100 random patches per image during pre-training). It is pre-trained 20 epochs on 9.18M LXMERT image-text pairs with masked LM, image-text matching and QA losses, with the CLIP ResNet unfrozen (SGD), then fine-tuned on VQA, SNLI-VE and GQA.

results: In VLN, swapping ImageNet-ResNet152 for CLIP-Res50x4 in EnvDrop raises R2R test-unseen to SR 59 / SPL 53. That beats the EnvDrop baseline (51/47), all non-pre-trained agents (best RelGraph 55/52) and PREVALENT (54/51), but stays below VLN-BERT (63/57). On RxR test-unseen (mono-lingual) it reaches SR 38.3 / nDTW 51.1 vs SAA 35.4/46.8. On R2R validation, the gains over ImageNet-Res152 are +6.5 SR (agent, 48.2→54.7) and +5.7 SR (BT-agent, 53.5→59.2). Beyond VLN, CLIP-ViLp with CLIP-Res50x4 sets SotA on VQA v2 (76.70 test-std, beating VinVL 76.12) and SNLI-VE (80.20 test), and CLIP-ViL gives +6.5 CIDEr on COCO captioning.
limitations: The VLN study only swaps frozen, pre-extracted CLIP features into a simple LSTM EnvDrop agent. It does not combine CLIP with VLN-specific pre-training, so it still trails VLN-BERT (63/57 on R2R test).
CLIP used zero-shot is near chance on VQA. CLIP-ViT-B grid features localize poorly (VG detection AP 0.03), which hurts grid-based tasks, and standard VG detection fine-tuning degrades CLIP-Res50.
CLIP-ViLp underperforms region-based VinVL on GQA and remains below Oscar/VinVL on captioning; the VLN table splits are not explicitly labeled.
